text:
mohit: heads up — customer (acme) reporting intermittent 504s followed by duplicate retries. they upgraded to go-sdk v1.4.2 yesterday and now see request latency spikes and a growth in goroutines. suspect interplay between context cancel + http.Client.Timeout + retry middleware.

james: thanks — any sample logs or a tiny repro?

mohit: pasted a trimmed log snippet from their app: 
```
2024-11-28T15:12:10Z caller=client.go request_id=abcd status=504 err="context canceled"
2024-11-28T15:12:10Z caller=retry.go attempt=2 request_id=abcd -> retrying
2024-11-28T15:12:10Z caller=client.go request_id=efgh status=200 latency=120ms
2024-11-28T15:12:12Z caller=client.go request_id=ijkl status=504 err="context canceled"
```

mohit: their client code pattern is basically: 
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
client := &http.Client{Timeout: 5 * time.Second}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// retry middleware wraps Do and retries on 5xx/timeout
```

james: ok — classic mismatch: per-request context 2s, client.Timeout 5s, plus retry wrapper that reuses the same transport/connection. when ctx is canceled the request returns an error, but we still see transport goroutines stuck in http2 read loops in their pprof. can you repro locally with small harness?

mohit: yes, I wrote a small harness that spins 200 goroutines hitting our hosted endpoint with artificial 600ms server delays and the retry wrapper (max 3 attempts). after ~30s goroutines climb steadily. stack dump shows lots of frames in net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop and golang.org/x/net/http2.(*clientConn).readFrame.

elaine: what Go and net/http versions are they on?

mohit: go1.20.6, net/http default. replace go-sdk with older v1.3.8 and the growth is much smaller. v1.4.3 (unreleased for them) has a change to how we create transports for per-request contexts (we switched to reusing a shared Transport but ensuring Request.WithContext is used consistently).

james: short-term mitigation options:
- stop setting client.Timeout and rely solely on Request context timeouts (safer for per-request cancellation).
- set Transport.DisableKeepAlives = true for a quick repro to see if connection reuse is the culprit (will increase TCP churn).
- reduce retry concurrency / add jitter to backoff.

mohit: asked customer to try removing client.Timeout and rerun. they reported fewer goroutines but still occasional spikes.

sasha: sounds like we should escalate to eng-runtime. filing an incident with reproduction steps and pprof. include: minimal repro app, exact SDK version, Go version, pprof, and the logs above.

mohit: repro steps I saved for the ticket: 
1) small program (attached) that does 200 concurrent requests to our echo endpoint. server returns 600ms delay and 500 on first attempt.
2) go-sdk v1.4.2 + retry middleware (retry up to 3 times instant backoff)
3) client uses context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second) + http.Client{Timeout: 5*time.Second}
4) run for 60s and capture goroutine profiles every 10s: look for many stuck in http2 readFrame or persistConn.readLoop.

mohit: snippet of the harness (trimmed): 
```
for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
  go func() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    _, _ = sdkClient.Call(ctx, payload)
  }()
}
time.Sleep(60 * time.Second)
pprof.WriteGoroutineProfile(f)
```

elaine: thanks. James, can you take a quick look at transport reuse logic in the retry wrapper? specifically whether we ever clone Transports per-call or mutate them. also confirm that sdk doesn't set a Transport.IdleConnTimeout to an insanely long value.

james: will do. initial glance: retry wrapper reuses the same http.Client instance across calls (by design). the problematic pattern is mixing client.Timeout with per-call contexts and retries that re-issue requests on canceled contexts. we should ensure our retry wrapper cancels any in-flight attempts cleanly and doesn't hold references to the request body or response body readers.

sasha: created ticket #SUP-5421 with attachments (pprof, harness, logs). tagging eng-runtime.

infra-bot: ticket SUP-5421 created and assigned to eng-runtime; priority P2.

mohit: customer will try quick config changes (remove client.Timeout, add small jitter) and we will follow up. thanks all. :thumbsup:
